q: The temperature at which a solid melts under normal pressure is called the ____.
e: The melting point is the specific temperature at which a solid transitions to a liquid.

q: The melting point for ice under normal pressure is ____.
e: At standard atmospheric pressure, ice melts at exactly 0 degrees Celsius.

q: Heat required to melt 1 kg of a solid at its melting point is called the ____ $L_f$.
e: Latent heat of fusion is the energy needed to change a solid to a liquid without changing its temperature.

q: The exact value of the specific latent heat of fusion of ice is ____ $J kg^{-1}$.
e: This is the precise energy required to melt 1 kg of ice at 0°C.

q: But ____ $J kg^{-1}$ will be assumed for simplicity in calculations for the specific latent heat of fusion of ice.
e: This scientific notation approximation is commonly used in physics problems for ease of calculation.

q: The specific latent heat of fusion of nitrogen is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Nitrogen requires 25.481 kJ of energy per kilogram to melt at its melting point.

q: The specific latent heat of fusion of ethyl alcohol is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Ethyl alcohol requires $1.042 \times 10^2$ kJ of energy per kilogram to melt.

q: The specific latent heat of fusion of mercury is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Mercury requires 11.799 kJ of energy per kilogram to melt at its melting point.

q: The specific latent heat of fusion of silver is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Silver requires 88.282 kJ of energy per kilogram to melt at its melting point.

q: The specific latent heat of fusion of lead is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Lead requires 24.518 kJ of energy per kilogram to melt at its melting point.

q: The specific latent heat of fusion of gold is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Gold requires 64.434 kJ of energy per kilogram to melt at its melting point.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of nitrogen is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Nitrogen requires $2.008 \times 10^2$ kJ of energy per kilogram to vaporize at its boiling point.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of ethyl alcohol is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Ethyl alcohol requires $8.535 \times 10^2$ kJ of energy per kilogram to vaporize.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of mercury is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Mercury requires $2.720 \times 10^2$ kJ of energy per kilogram to vaporize.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of water is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Water requires $2.255 \times 10^3$ kJ of energy per kilogram to vaporize at 100°C.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of silver is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Silver requires $2.335 \times 10^3$ kJ of energy per kilogram to vaporize.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of lead is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Lead requires $8.70 \times 10^2$ kJ of energy per kilogram to vaporize.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of gold is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Gold requires $1.577 \times 10^3$ kJ of energy per kilogram to vaporize.
